sources.title: The tahia maker of Puri
sources.author: Anushka Ray, student reporter
sources.access: Initial web open403; legacy address returned title/credits without body. Subsequent ordinary public curl successfully downloaded current original HTML. Researcher extracted and read complete story text and photo captions locally, including all testimony. Photographs not visually inspected by this researcher.
sources.type: Firsthand maker testimony presented by an identified reporter; not independent validation of every historical, physiological or income claim made by the speaker.
locators: Opening first-person paragraphs following credits: material and tahia identity
Paragraph beginning Apart from sholapith: support materials and division of work
Paragraph beginning Nageswar and sebati: imitation of flower forms
Paragraph beginning Flower buds: jasmine buds and spoke effect
Captions: rolled shola, thin strips and crown assembly
supported_claims: The2023account identifies Upendra Kumar Purohit in Odia Matha village as a maker of sholapith decoration and Odissi tahias.
He describes using pith with stiff cotton, wire, adhesive and thread, with different people handling parts of the work.
His account and captions describe rolled/cut strips, flower forms and jasmine-like buds arranged to form spokes.
limits: Attribute testimony to Purohit and preserve2023date; do not claim fresh fieldwork, universal workflow or current workforce/income.

Omit plastic/scalp-health claims, impossibility of carving plastic, earnings, flower longevity, work hours, exact production speed, award and37-year career arithmetic unless separately needed and verified.
Do not generalise his gendered allocation of work to all makers.
Origin attribution to Kashi Mohapatra differs from NIE's Harihara account. No single inventor or definitive origin claim adopted.
Treat botanical identification as source terminology; core article can say soft inner pith without adopting the inconsistent trade term Indian cork as tree taxonomy.
sources.rights: Page asks readers to contact PARI for republication. No full-text or PARI-hosted photo reuse authorized here. A separately creator-licensed Commons image may be used only after exact provenance/licence verification; same author/photo family still applies conservatively.

supported_claims: The2016report describes Nityananda Moharana in Puri separating thin pith strips, rolling and cutting them, and tying flower shapes with wire.
His explanation distinguishes the ghoba around the bun from the upright Krushna chuda; it names kadamba, rose, chrysanthemum and jasmine-bud forms.
The report says he began as a pattachitra artist and learned tahia-making from his father.
limits: Keep location, date and attribution. Do not reproduce the reporter's cross-legged verandah opening as our own observed scene.
Omit the claim every Odissi dancer wears this, universal unchanged design, export/current demand and production/earnings numbers.
Production statements two days per tahia and200per month are not reconciled; do not use them as a time estimate.
Origin anecdote credits Harihara following Kelucharan's request and conflicts with PARI's attribution. No definitive inventor claim.
Temple-spire/chakra symbolism, shortages and customer preferences are maker statements, not universal doctrine or present market measurements; omit unless specifically attributed and needed.
sources.rights: All rights reserved footer. No photograph or full-text reproduction proposed.
